title: Drain choreography with lease windows and autoscaler contracts
creator: Marcus O'Hare
description:
Background: Upgrades to dedicated GPU pools currently rely on simplistic drain flows that trigger aggressive eviction followed by autoscaler activity. In practice we've observed transient SLA degradation during waves (observed in recent canaries) due to autoscaler thrash and inability to reserve soft capacity for inflight rollouts. This ticket implements a coordinated drain choreography that introduces timeboxed lease windows and an autoscaler contract (handshake) so upgrades can reserve transient capacity, apply soft-drain semantics, and avoid admission spikes.

Objectives:
- Introduce a lease token API so the upgrade controller can request short-lived capacity reservations (soft buffers) from the autoscaler.
- Implement temporal safety windows (lease window: start/hold/handback) so drains proceed in phases (prefix-cache preservation -> soft-evict -> hard-evict) with measurable thresholds at each phase.
- Add backpressure signals to the admission controller so traffic routing respects ongoing drains and does not redirect sudden bursts to draining pools.
- Provide observability: per-pool rollout state, held lease tokens, admission backpressure meters, and incident alerts when capacity headroom < configured floor.

Proposed approach:
1) Autoscaler contract: minimal REST/gRPC handshake: request_lease(pool, seats, duration) -> response(accepted|rejected, granted_seats, expiry). Autoscaler enforces lease accounting against committed capacity and responds with one of three statuses: accepted (grant), queued (deferred), rejected.
2) Upgrade choreography state machine: prepare -> reserve (request_lease) -> soft_drain (evict idle/preferred) -> monitor (metrics & headroom check) -> escalate (hard_drain) -> release_lease -> verification. Each transition has timers and SLO gates.
3) Admission/backpressure: augment fronting proxies to lower route weights to pools in soft_drain based on a backpressure score computed from eviction progress and pinned KV cache hit ratios.
4) Safety nets: global rollout rate cap, per-tenant minimum slices, automatic bailout to fallback pools when headroom < emergency_threshold, and canary-only mode before full rollout.

Success metrics:
- 99.9th percentile latency for affected tenant requests does not regress during a full fleet wave (target: < 5% change).
- Peak request admission drop during upgrades <= 2% of baseline.
- No increase in error rate attributable to container preemption/eviction during rollout.
- Automated rollout completes within expected window 95% of the time; lease-rejection rate < 5% under normal load.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Design review and API spec for lease contract + state machine.
- Week 2: PoC autoscaler side accounting + simulated grants in staging.
- Week 3: Integrate controller to request/reserve/release leases; implement soft_drain path.
- Week 4: Admission proxy backpressure integration + observability dashboards/alerts.
- Week 5: Canary rollout across low-traffic pools and soak.

Rollout safeguards and rollback plan:
- Start in canary mode with very small slices (1-2% of fleet). If metrics breach gates, controller auto-aborts and releases leases; autoscaler revokes queued grants.
- Rollout controller supports incremental rollback per-pool and forced immediate release of leases on emergency.
- Post-incident runbook created and linked in attachments.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Lease windows add complexity and slightly increased coupling between upgrade controller and autoscaler; mitigated by small, well-documented API and conservative defaults.
- Admission backpressure changes require careful tuning to avoid request routing oscillation; initial rollout uses slow-moving decay constants and manual tuning in staging.

Operational artifacts: see attachments for design doc, runbook, PRs and dashboards.
comments: 2026-03-02 Marcus O'Hare: Triage complete. Identified recurrent issue: autoscaler latency + aggressive eviction causing transient SLA blips during waves. Assigning to Lina for implementation exploration.

2026-03-04 Lina Park: Drafted API contract for lease tokens. Shared in #infra-release for early feedback. Key open Q: should leases be hard-guarantees or soft reservations? Proposal: soft reservations with expiry and optional preemption for emergency.

2026-03-05 Alex Chen (Infra Eng): Reviewed API draft. Concern: accounting race between multiple concurrent controllers requesting leases. Suggested using monotonic counters and idempotency keys. Added to design doc.

2026-03-08 Lina Park: PoC landed in staging: basic request_lease endpoint + simple accounting. Load-tested with synthetic traffic. Results: grant latency median 8ms, P99 95ms under normal load. P99 acceptable for now; will optimize.

2026-03-09 QA (Priya Singh): Integration smoke in staging with canary controller. Observed backpressure smoothing works but cache-hit preservation needs tuning — KV cache eviction during soft_drain is higher than expected. Added follow-up task.

2026-03-10 Lina Park: Opened PRs: fleet-upgrades#789 (controller state machine + lease usage), autoscaler#412 (lease accounting). Requesting review from @AlexChen and @Marta Ruiz. Added dashboard panels for lease grants and headroom.

2026-03-11 Alex Chen: Code review feedback left on autoscaler#412: ensure idempotent lease release and add metric 'lease_rejections' with labels by pool and reason. Also recommended a feature flag to gate soft_drain behavior.

2026-03-12 Lina Park: Addressed review feedback; added feature flag rollout and emergency bailout path. Preparing canary to run next week. Next actions: tuning KV eviction threshold and runbook drills with SRE.
2026-03-12 SRE (Marta Ruiz): Created incident playbook entry and scheduled tabletop for 2026-03-18 to rehearse rollback and lease-revoke flows.
